_description: Fixture 2 — Contradictions present. Tests contradiction detection metric. Two claims have contradicting evidence.
research_question: Does intermittent fasting improve metabolic health markers in adults?

report.executive_summary: Intermittent fasting has been shown to improve insulin sensitivity and reduce fasting glucose levels in several randomized controlled trials. [SOURCE 1] However, some studies report no significant metabolic improvement compared to continuous caloric restriction. [SOURCE 2]
key_findings: 16:8 time-restricted eating reduced fasting insulin levels by 20% over 12 weeks. [SOURCE 1]
A meta-analysis found intermittent fasting and continuous caloric restriction produce equivalent weight loss. [SOURCE 2]
Alternate-day fasting improved LDL cholesterol by 15% in overweight adults. [SOURCE 3]
Intermittent fasting eliminates all metabolic benefit compared to standard diet according to a 2022 RCT. [SOURCE 4]
report.limitations: Most trials are short-term (< 6 months) with small sample sizes.

evidence.content: In a 12-week RCT, participants following 16:8 time-restricted eating experienced a 20% reduction in fasting insulin levels (p<0.01) compared to unrestricted eating controls.

A systematic review and meta-analysis of 27 RCTs found no statistically significant difference in weight loss, BMI reduction, or metabolic markers between intermittent fasting and continuous caloric restriction (p=0.72).
Overweight adults (BMI 27–35) following alternate-day fasting for 8 weeks showed a mean LDL cholesterol reduction of 15.2 mg/dL (p<0.05) compared to baseline.

A 2022 RCT with 116 participants found no significant difference in insulin sensitivity, HbA1c, or fasting glucose between intermittent fasting and standard dietary advice groups after 6 months (all p>0.20).

claims.claim_text: 16:8 time-restricted eating reduced fasting insulin levels by 20% over 12 weeks.
A meta-analysis found intermittent fasting and continuous caloric restriction produce equivalent weight loss.
Alternate-day fasting improved LDL cholesterol by 15% in overweight adults.
Intermittent fasting eliminates all metabolic benefit compared to standard diet.
claims._note: The claim is contradicted: ev-02-a shows insulin benefit, ev-02-c shows LDL benefit. The 'all benefit eliminated' claim overstates ev-02-d.
